items.question: What was the assisting tug Steel Skipper doing when the William E Strait ended up backing into barges tied up at the Shell refinery pier near Norco?
items.expected_answer: The Steel Skipper was reconfiguring the William E Strait's tow and pushed the tow astern, so the William E Strait struck two moored barges upstream at the Shell Norco Refinery dock.

evidence.quote: when the towing vessel Steel Skipper, which was reconfiguring the tow, pushed the tow astern, and the William E Strait collided with two moored barges upstream at the Shell Norco Refinery dock, damaging the barges and dock

items.notes: Tests the tug's action during the casualty; the casualty summary table itself holds no procedural content, so the evidence comes from the opening summary paragraph above it.

items.question: During the barge shuffling near Norco, where was the William E Strait's mate stationed, and did he try using propulsion to keep clear of the barges tied up behind his boat?
items.expected_answer: The mate was on the bridge; because he did not recognize the danger of hitting the moored barges and dock aft of the tow, he did not use his engines to try to avoid them.

evidence.quote: the mate, who was on the bridge at the time, did not recognize that his vessel was in danger of colliding with the moored barges and dock aft of the tow, and therefore did not use his engines to attempt to avoid them.

items.notes: Tests the mate's (in)action as described in the analysis section.
